beats.narration_text: Liam, in for Bear — part three. Structure and depth: the H and AI glyphs counter-rotate in a ligature spotlight, each letter card-flips on its X axis in sequence, a scale focus pushes from the full word into a single glyph and back, and a blur rack focuses front to back across the word. These moves reveal what the wordmark is made of.

Let's recap with Claude. Ligature spotlight: the leading H and the diagonal counter-rotate — only words with an internal relationship can do this. Per-letter flip: each glyph cards on its X axis in sequence. Scale focus: full word in, single glyph out, back. Blur rack: sharpness travels across the word like rack focus through a lens. Structure is the subject.

Your turn. Paste this: push a scale focus from the full HUMANITARIANS AI wordmark into a single glyph — the H — then pull back out — and tell me which glyph is worth this zoom. Not every glyph earns an iris-in. The H earns it.
H A I wordmark, in motion. Part three. Liam, in for Bear.
